continuationDomain.sourceRef: BOTH halves. Own-state acceptance: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content/thought-signatures (read 2026-10-29), "Signatures for OpenAI compatibility": each `tool_calls` entry carries `"extra_content": {"google": {"thought_signature": "<Signature A>"}}`, sent back on the same entry ("Required and Validated"); in a parallel batch only the first call carries one. https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai: "Gemini 3 supports OpenAI compatibility for thought signatures in chat completion APIs." The Chat Completions adapter captures `extra_content` per call id on this connection and replays it on that call. Why the domain is NARROW: the state is valid only for the model that produced it on this route -- a different model, or the same model at another provider (a different credential and account), never receives it, and the history renderer strips it there.

replayScope.sourceRef: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content/thought-signatures (read 2026-10-29): "Strict validation is enforced for all function calls within the current turn. (Only current turn is required; we don't validate on previous turns)"

toolLoopRequirement.sourceRef: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content/thought-signatures (read 2026-10-29): "When using Gemini 4 and Gemini 3 models, you must pass back thought signatures during function calling, otherwise you will get a validation error (4xx status code)"; "Function call `FC1` in the `1.` content block is missing a `thought_signature`"

Own-state acceptance: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content/thought-signatures (read 2026-10-29), "Signatures for OpenAI compatibility": each `tool_calls` entry carries `"extra_content": {"google": {"thought_signature": "<Signature A>"}}`, sent back on the same entry ("Required and Validated"); in a parallel batch only the first call carries one. https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai: "Gemini 3 supports OpenAI compatibility for thought signatures in chat completion APIs." The Chat Completions adapter captures `extra_content` per call id on this connection and replays it on that call. Why the domain is NARROW: the state is valid only for the model that produced it on this route -- a different model, or the same model at another provider (a different credential and account), never receives it, and the history renderer strips it there.

replayScope.sourceRef: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content/thought-signatures (read 2026-10-29): "Strict validation is enforced for all function calls within the current turn. (Only current turn is required; we don't validate on previous turns)"

toolLoopRequirement.sourceRef: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content/thought-signatures (read 2026-10-29): "When using Gemini 4 and Gemini 3 models, you must pass back thought signatures during function calling, otherwise you will get a validation error (4xx status code)"; "Function call `FC1` in the `1.` content block is missing a `thought_signature`"

pricing.sourceRef: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (read 2026-10-29) — Gemini 4 Argon, Standard, Paid Tier per 1M tokens in USD: Input price "$2.00 through November 30, 2026. $4.00 starting December 1, 2026."; Output price (including thinking tokens) "$10.00 through November 30, 2026. $20.00 starting December 1, 2026."; Context caching price "$0.10 through November 30, 2026. $0.20 starting December 1, 2026. Implicit caching only (explicit caching is not supported)." TIERED IN TIME, which `ModelPricing` cannot express: the CURRENT (through 2026-11-30) introductory rate is recorded, so from 2026-12-01 this row UNDER-reports by exactly 2x on every field until it is re-priced — the same disclosed gap as google/gemini-3.8-flash. No long-context tier is published for this model (flat across the 1M window); "Gemini 4 Argon is not available on the Free tier." Batch/Flex (50%) and Priority are separate rate cards and are not folded in; no cache-write rate is published, so that key is absent.
